density functional theory

Ye-Hua Jiang*

Abstract The chemical stability, electronic structures,
mechanical properties and Debye temperature of Fe–Mn–
Al alloys were investigated using first-principles calcula-
tions. The formation enthalpy and cohesive energy are
negative for Fe–Mn–Al alloys, showing that they are
thermodynamically stable. FeAl has the lowest formation
enthalpy, indicating that FeAl is the most stable alloy in the
Fe–Mn–Al system. The partial density of states, total
density of states and electron density distribution maps
were used to analyze the physical properties of the Fe–Mn–
Al alloys. A combination of mainly covalent and metallic
bonds exists in these Fe–Mn–Al alloys, resulting in good
electronic conductivity, high melting points, and high
hardness. These alloys display disparate anisotropy due to
the calculated different shapes of the 3D curved surface of
the Young’s modulus and anisotropic index. FeAl has the
highest bulk modulus, shear modulus and Yong’s modulus
of 187.1, 119.8 and 296.2 GPa, respectively. Further, the
Debye temperatures and sound velocity of these Fe–Mn–Al
compounds were explored.
Keywords Fe–Mn–Al alloys; Electronic structures;
Stability; Mechanical properties; Debye temperature; First-
principles calculation

4 Conclusion
In conclusion, the chemical stability, electronic structures,
anisotropic elastic properties and Debye temperature of
these Fe–Mn–Al alloys were investigated using first-prin-
ciples calculations. The cohesive energy and formation
enthalpy illustrate that they are thermodynamically stable.
The formation enthalpy value of FeAl is the lowest.
Therefore, FeAl is the most stable in the
\mathrm { F e } _ { 1 - x } \mathbf { M } \mathbf { n } _ { x } \mathbf { A } 1
system. The bonding features of the
\mathrm { F e } _ { 1 - x } \mathbf { M } \mathbf { n } _ { x } \mathbf { A } \mathbf { l }
system
are a combination of covalent bonds and metallic bonds,
which leads to good electronic conductivity, relatively high
melting points and high hardness. Several anisotropy
indexes were calculated to estimate the mechanical aniso-
tropy, indicating that MnAl has the strongest anisotropy.
These alloys have strong anisotropy characteristic in the
Young’s modulus. The change in the hardness and Debye
temperature follows a similar trend. FeAl has the highest
Debye temperature of 652.5 K, showing that FeAl has
stronger covalent bonds than other alloys.
